description: Master Services Agreement — US transactional norms

liability_cap.description: Aggregate liability cap should generally be at least 12 months of fees paid in the trailing period. Sub-12-month caps are aggressive in favor of Provider.
red_flags: liability cap of 3 months or less

indemnification.description: Mutual indemnification, with carve-outs for IP infringement and breach of confidentiality. One-way indemnification favoring Provider only is heavily Provider-friendly.

termination.description: Both parties should have termination rights. Termination for convenience by Provider without refund of prepaid fees is unusual. 30-day notice period is standard.
red_flags: termination for convenience without refund clause
notice period under 15 days for convenience termination

ip_ownership.description: Work product ownership should be clearly assigned to Customer (work-for-hire or assignment). Provider retains pre-existing IP and general tools/methodologies.
red_flags: no carve-out for Provider pre-existing IP

confidentiality.description: Tight definition of Confidential Information (marked or known to be confidential). Survival period 3-5 years post-termination is standard; perpetual for trade secrets.
red_flags: overly broad confidentiality definition (e.g., 'all information shared')

governing_law.description: Should specify a US state. Delaware, New York, and California are common neutral choices. Avoid offshore or non-US jurisdictions for US-based parties.
red_flags: non-US governing law for US parties
governing law in Provider home state without negotiation

dpa.description: Data Protection Addendum (DPA) required if Provider processes Customer personal data. Reference must exist in main agreement; DPA itself can be an exhibit.
red_flags: no DPA reference despite data processing
DPA reference but no executed DPA attached
DPA terms inconsistent with main agreement
